endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Establish and maintain a structured data acquisition register for data used in AI systems.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: ensure that guardrails are well defined and documented for who is approved to access a given dataset or data type, and for what purposes.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Dependencies between upstream, downstream, or other data, internet of things (IOT) or AI systems;

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: A description of the data storage of both training and test data.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Collect information on data provenance | Data centres, equipment characteristics, data preprocessing, annotation processes

endorsements.title: Towards responsible artificial intelligence in healthcare—getting real about real-world data and evidence
endorsements.quote: Metadata standards should be established from existing standards under the same Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) principles 12 recommended to characterize RWD sources, including provenance, context of creation, collection methods, coverage (ie, geographic, temporal, socio-demographic representativeness), and formats.

endorsements.title: Machine unlearning as a governance imperative for clinical AI
endorsements.quote: Teams must track where each training example influences deployed models, maintain version control for models and datasets, and reserve compute fo r deletion and re validation.

endorsements.title: Predictive fetal medicine and the ownership of prenatal data: legal, ethical, and professional challenges
endorsements.quote: Ethical governance must prevent retroactive data appropriation and maintain dual protection: maternal data remain confidential unless separable from fetal data; secondary use requires independent ethical oversight.

endorsements.title: AI in Clinical Decision Support Systems: Promising Applications and Strategies for Managing Data Challenges
endorsements.quote: Observability and lineage—trace where data came from, how they were transformed, and how they impact models to increase transparency and explainability, making processes understandable to clinicians and affected individuals.

endorsements.title: Pediatric Clinical Images Without Consent: A Governance Gap in the Long-Term Reuse of Health Data in Digital Health Ecosystems
endorsements.quote: Implement consent-linked metadata, provenance tracking, and interoperable removal protocols across platforms

endorsements.title: Promise, Mimicry, and Surveillance: Responsibly Integrating Artificial Intelligence With Socratic Inquiry in Medical Education
endorsements.quote: Before acquisition, institutions should adopt responsible-use principles such as those articulated by the Association of American Medical Colleges [ 10 ] and require the documented assessment of the specific educational gap being addressed; a data inventory specifying what is collected, how long it is retained, with whom it is shared, and when it is deleted [ 36 ]; system limitations and the thresholds at which a tool is withdrawn; a cost-benefit analysis that accounts for opportunity cost and the value of displaced educator time; and named actors accountable for ongoing audit.

commentary.bottom_line: Nine sources endorse an AI data register, including two CHAI frameworks at the must level and an FDA draft guidance at the should level, but no supplied study tests whether a register reduces use of untracked or unknown-origin data. The recommendation rests on expert consensus and commentary rather than measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: No study tests the practice, and no study documents the hazard's frequency or consequences. The nine endorsements include frameworks, guidance, and commentaries, and none of these designs yields an effect estimate. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. Agreement across sources shows consistent expert opinion, not demonstrated benefit.

The FDA draft guidance on AI-enabled device software asks sponsors to describe storage of training and test data, and NIST AI 600-1 asks organizations to track dependencies between upstream and downstream data and systems. A register may help organizations answer these requests. Neither document is final binding law for local deployers, and the draft status may change.

No supplied study examines the register in any population. Commentaries on prenatal and pediatric image data raise consent and secondary-use concerns for groups who cannot consent for themselves. These concerns suggest that sensitivity classes may need to capture consent status, but no evidence shows whether a register protects these groups.

commentary.research_gap: No study has compared organizations with and without an AI data register on outcomes such as unauthorized dataset use, time to trace data behind a model error, completeness of provenance records, consent-violation incidents, or staff burden to keep the register current. Studies of the hazard itself, including how often AI projects use data of unknown origin or rights, are also absent.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Organizations serving these groups have no evidence on whether a register affects data rights or harms for their patients, or on the cost of maintaining one with limited staff.
